chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: Lying in bed: no pain, just helplessness
summary: Asked about the frustration of bed rest, Cobb says there was little pain after the first days, just the dependence on nurses turning and rubbing him.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: (Inaudible). This is a sort of silly question that to ask you (inaudible), so, okay, you've got to lie there and all this time there's a sort of (inaudible) frustration and every-
Just the idea of having to lay in bed, be turned and rubbed down and not get bedsores and this sort of thing.
Sort of the helplessness of it.

Right. I, you know, your pain is mostly two or three days after the operation, and they give you something to relieve that. And I didn't want a lot of dope. If I could take it myself, I took as much as I could take, but after that I didn't have any pain.

Yeah, just a matter of time limit of laying. I was comfortable, and as long as I got the treatment, why they turned me over and rubbed my back and powder me down, pat me on the behind. These are things I needed for self consolation. And I got that. I got that.
